messages:
incidents-bot: INCIDENT 1799995000 — KV_CACHE_REUSE_HIGH detected in prod-us-east-1. Error rate spike on runtime-service: continuous-batching pipeline showing stale KV hits and sequence offset mismatches. Auto-severity: P2. Paging on-call. @sara oncall
sara: ack — investigating. hitting dashboard now. symptoms? customer reports? :mag:
incidents-bot: Top symptoms: token corruption (wrong persona), occasional cross-request token reuse, tail latency spike. 12 errors/min across 3 clusters. Affected models: rdlw-13b-qa-v2 and rdlw-7b-chat (quantized). Sample trace ids attached to alert.
ken: on it. I can reproduce locally with stress harness by sending interleaved streaming requests that hit cached KV ranges. I see KV entries with seq_offset 0 for later requests — looks like reuse of cache shard without seq bump.
sara: can you paste the failing snippet? I'm checking if this matches yesterday's batch config tilt.
ken: here's a simplified repro log:
```
REQUEST id=abc123 model=rdlw-13b-qa-v2 seq=42
KV_LOOKUP shard=3 key=ctx-7 -> cached_offset=40
EMIT tokens from offset 40 (should be 42) => overlap
```
This is not just stale value, it's wrong seq pointer being returned from cache.
alex: any recent rollout touching KV sharders or cache LRU? I rolled the compactor yesterday in prod-us-east-1 at 03:10UTC but that was metadata-only.
sara: batching config changed in the last deploy? maybe continuous-batching reuse enabled a new codepath.
ken: right — config flag continuous_kv_reuse=true was toggled for a/b experiments on a subset of pods. It looks like the reuse path has a race where shard->last_seq isn't updated before being published to other workers.
sara: impact estimate? which customers may have seen leaks/personal data mixing?
ken: early telemetry shows ~0.04% of requests returned non-monotonic seqs; of those, ~30% included tokens from previous conversation. That's ~0.012% of overall requests. There are a handful of long-lived sessions customers hitting high token rates — they likely saw more.
ops-bot: Alert: customer-387 (enterprise) opened support ticket referencing mixed context in generations. Severity: medium.
sara: ok. mitigation suggestions?
ken: immediate options:
- hotfix A: disable continuous_kv_reuse flag at runtime via config rollout (fast, safe)
- hotfix B: clear kv shard cache version token (potentially disruptive) — requires rolling restarts
- hotfix C: apply patch to atomic update ordering (dev-cycle longer)
I propose hotfix A now to stop further reuse while we patch.
alex: I can flip the flag via k8s configmap for runtime-service-prod in us-east-1; will target canary first then global. ETA ~6m for canary rollout.
sara: do it. @alex please include a note to ops-channel when done. Also add temporary tracing to log seq diffs for 1 hour.
alex: doing canary now. command:
```
kubectl -n prod patch configmap runtime-config --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/data/continuous_kv_reuse","value":"false"}]'
```
canary applied to pods runtime-1, runtime-2. monitoring for errors.
ops-bot: Canary logs: error-rate on canary decreased from 12/min to 1/min within 2m. Latency normalized.
sara: proceed with global rollout once canary looks good. ken keep collecting traces for root cause.
ken: collecting. I'm seeing that the reuse path omits increment of the per-shard seq watermark under high interleaving when batch flushes concurrently. Will instrument commit ordering.
maria: heads up — I'm stepping in for the next 2 hours (handoff). @sara handing off after rollout. Please include me on commands and escalation.
sara: thanks @maria. I'm going to push global now.
alex: global patch applied to us-east-1. command triggered rolling restart with config propagate. watching.
incidents-bot: Runtime checks show KV reuse metric dropping to near-zero across all us-east-1 runtime nodes.
sara: good. now we need to mitigate customer impact and communicate. @ken can you run a quick scan for any logs that show PII exposure? we need list of affected requests and customers to notify SRE incident comms.
ken: running log query for traces with non-monotonic seqs and token overlap. rough results: ~450 traces in the last 3 hours, mapped to ~28 unique customer orgs, 4 flagged as high-privacy (long prompts). I'll hand to security for review.
ops-bot: Ticket created: #INC-1799995000-customer-impact with attached trace ids and counts.
sara: status update for stakeholders: mitigation applied (continuous_kv_reuse disabled), error-rate reduced, investigation ongoing. I'll draft a customer-safe blurb.
alex: one more thing — we should consider a config gate that enforces per-shard seq atomic commit; I'll open a quick RFC.
ken: dev patch almost ready; core fix is to add an atomic CAS when publishing last_seq and ensure any reader sees updated seq before reuse. I'll run tests & canary tomorrow.
maria: oncall handoff note: monitoring alert thresholds lowered to catch any reappearance. If we see >1/min anomaly re-escalate to P1.
sara: current status: mitigation success, postmortem required. next steps:
- ken to PR fix and unit tests (owner: ken)
- alex to codify config rollback runbook (owner: alex)
- sara to draft customer comms and coordinate legal/ops (owner: sara)
- maria to monitor and close incident after 24h of clean metrics
sara: thanks all. @ken please attach sample failing traces (scrubbed) to the postmortem doc.
ken: will do. quick note: hotfix caused minimal disruption — slight increase in token cost due to reduced reuse but acceptable.
incidents-bot: INCIDENT 1799995000 status: mitigated — reduced severity to P3. Auto-assigning follow-up tasks channel #postmortems.
maria: handing off to @sara for postmortem, I'm available if it flares. :white_check_mark:
sara: closing thread here, will open postmortem doc in product/eng channels with timeline and RCA. Thanks team. :heart:
